clue.text: Tory leader managed to get a month on the wing

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the party word is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the party name
to run a business is to manage it
the short form of September

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief secures a month's place on the party's wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing' is the political wing in the surface, but the definition is a wing of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: In a cross-shaped church, each arm crossing the nave is called a transept, its side wing.

clue.text: Record that's broken when record is broken

definitions.text: that's broken when record is broken

blocks.note: first meaning: to record sound or a programme on a cassette

blocks.clueFragment: that's broken when record is broken
blocks.note: second meaning: the finishing strip a runner breaks when winning a race

explanation.walkthrough: Record is a verb first, then a noun about a sporting best; the strip across the finish line is breasted by the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic recording medium and the ribbon stretched across the finish line share one short word.

clue.text: Early victim - a Babylonian idol

blocks.note: taken as written
Bel was a chief god of Babylon

explanation.surface: An ancient statue of a god was among the first to fall.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Cain's brother was murdered, the first homicide victim in the Bible.

clue.text: Coy smile makes MP rise

indicators.note: makes here means forms or builds, so the following letters are built into a new word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shy grin from someone causes a politician to stand up in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To simper is to give a silly, affected smile, often coy or self-conscious.

clue.text: Familiar tapes played by Dad

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Father runs the same old cassettes again.
explanation.definitionFit: A paterfamilias is the male head of a household, the father of the family.

clue.text: Disorder arising from a maths problem

indicators.note: a problem is something worked out, so the letters before it are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical condition supposedly brought on by a tricky arithmetic question.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory complaint, a chronic disorder of the airways causing breathlessness.

clue.text: Waste in herb medication

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits within the other, here the medication within the herb

blocks.note: sage is a common herb
a pill is a tablet of medicine

explanation.surface: Wasted drugs found inside a herbal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spillage is the amount spilt and lost, which is waste.

clue.text: Middle England carrying light suit?

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so the suit word holds the word for light

blocks.note: hearts is one of the four card suits
to light on a place is to alight or land there

explanation.surface: The central shires toting a lightweight outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light suit' reads as summer clothing; 'light' is the verb meaning come down, and suit means a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartlands are the central or core regions, so Middle England is the nation's heartland.

clue.text: A (provisional appointment)

blocks.note: surface reading: a bracketed note that someone is merely a temporary appointee
setter's reading: the letter A is at the front of the clue, temporarily heading it, and stands in for a deputy boss

explanation.walkthrough: The letter A begins the clue, so it is its head, and the bracket says the post is only temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy filling a vacant post until a permanent principal is chosen holds a temporary appointment.

clue.text: Man injured in cup-tie riot could be blown up

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so the first word gets rearranged
a riot is disorder, so the hyphenated word joins the jumble

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A football fan hurt in crowd trouble at a cup match might need inflating or be at risk of an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' suggests an explosion at the riot; here it means filled with air, as a tyre is.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumatic describes something filled or worked by compressed air, such as an inflated tyre.

clue.text: Landlord in London, perhaps, found after a full

blocks.note: London is an example of a capital city
a landlord is one who lets property

explanation.surface: A London landlord turns up after a complete something.
explanation.walkthrough: A landlord in London is literally a 'capital letter'. The definition stops short: what comes after a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentences begin with an upper-case character, so one appears after every full stop.

clue.text: It's not suitable to sleep in it

indicators.note: the word for sleep is placed inside the final word of the clue

blocks.note: taken as written
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A warning that bedding down in some place is improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means inappropriate or ill-fitting, a direct synonym of unsuitable.

clue.text: Primatial line?

blocks.note: surface reading: a line of succession among church primates, archbishops
setter's reading: an archbishop's title that is also the name of a London Underground route

explanation.walkthrough: A metropolitan is an archbishop heading a province; the Metropolitan is a line on the London Underground, the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a senior archbishop, whose rank is primatial, and a famous railway route in London.

clue.text: No vista all round from this side

indicators.note: turning round suggests the letters are spun into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: From this viewpoint you can see nothing in any direction.
explanation.walkthrough: A side is a sports team; this is a Birmingham football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is an English football club, and a team is often called a side.

clue.text: Two score win over thousands in nap

blocks.note: a score is twenty
taken as written
K is the abbreviation for a thousand, made plural

explanation.surface: A gambler wins twice by twenty over thousands of pounds by napping, a tip to back a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for a brief daytime doze is an idiom for a short sleep.

clue.text: Rest period

blocks.note: first meaning: a halt or pause
second meaning: the punctuation mark ending a sentence, a full one

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like one phrase about a break time, but each separately defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A halt in movement is a pause, and a full point in punctuation is called a full stop or period.

clue.text: One gets power from above

blocks.note: surface reading: someone granted authority by heaven or by a superior
setter's reading: the hinged frame on a train or tram roof that collects current from overhead wires

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds divine or political; it is really about electric trains picking up current from cables overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: This hinged collector arm on electric locomotives presses against the overhead wire to draw electricity.

clue.text: Cover for higher education classes

blocks.note: short for university
school classes are called forms in Britain

explanation.surface: Insurance protecting university and school classes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a class or year group is a form.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard outfits worn by pupils or staff clothe the body, so they serve as a cover.

clue.text: Nothing judicious worn by model for show

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone wraps around them, so the word for judicious goes round the model

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
a judicious decision is a sensible one
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A fashion model sporting nothing sensible, merely for display.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T Ford is the crossword's usual source of T for model.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done for show is ostensible: apparent or professed rather than genuine.

clue.text: Girl from east and going west

indicators.note: in an across entry west is leftward, so the joining word is read from right to left

blocks.note: the compass abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman who has travelled from the east and is now heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a female forename, and crosswords often define a name by the word girl.

clue.text: A sign of balance

blocks.note: first meaning: Libra, the zodiac sign pictured as a weighing device
second meaning: a weighing apparatus

explanation.walkthrough: 'A sign of balance' sounds like an indication of stability; the two parts separately define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra is drawn as a pair of weighing pans, and a weighing balance is also called this.

clue.text: Unspoken promise?

blocks.note: surface reading: an implicit, unstated understanding between people
setter's reading: a solemn pledge, as taken by monks, never to talk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unspoken' suggests a tacit agreement; instead the pledge itself is to stay mute.
explanation.definitionFit: Some religious orders take a solemn pledge to refrain from talking, which is literally a promise about not speaking.

clue.text: Cabinet minister's transport?

indicators.note: a cabinet is a cupboard that holds things, so the next word holds the answer inside it

blocks.note: the opening four letters of the word

explanation.surface: The official car laid on for a member of the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' looks like the government's inner circle; here it is a cupboard holding the start of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is a classic small British car, a means of getting about.

clue.text: Accustom to doing without Guardian article

blocks.note: a newspaper's editorials speak as we
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Getting used to life without the newspaper and its features.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian, the British newspaper that publishes this puzzle, refers to itself in editorials as we.
explanation.definitionFit: To wean a child or animal is to get it used to managing without its mother's milk.

clue.text: Solitary individual caught between opposing sides

indicators.note: something caught between two things sits inside them, so the word for individual goes in the middle

blocks.note: left and right, the two opposite sides
a single individual is one

explanation.surface: A lone person trapped in the middle of a quarrel between two camps.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a solitary is a recluse, someone who keeps apart from others.

clue.text: TV providing little as possible energy

indicators.note: possible suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A television service supplying as little energy as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiting relay craft beams television broadcasts down to dishes, so it is a TV provider.

clue.text: Balaam's mount in need of first aid

blocks.note: in the Bible, Balaam rode a donkey that spoke to him
1st with the numeral read as the letter I

explanation.surface: The Bible's talking donkey requires emergency medical attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First aid' reads as one phrase, but 'first' belongs to the wordplay and 'aid' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is to help or support them, which is to assist.

clue.text: Nastier form of government toady

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the first word is reshaped into another

blocks.note: taken as written
in casual and dialect speech 'of' shrinks to 'a', as in 'cup a tea'

explanation.surface: A meaner type of state flunkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like a link word, but it must supply the eighth letter: dictionaries such as Chambers list 'a' as a colloquial form of 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Erastian holds that the state should rule over the church, a doctrine deferring to secular rulers.
